The Cotswolds: England's Gentlest Touring Paradise

The Cotswolds offers a completely different motorcycle experience from the mountain passes and dramatic coastlines found elsewhere in Britain. Here, the pleasure is in gentle, flowing roads through honey-stone villages, rolling farmland, and ancient market towns. It's touring at its most civilised — and utterly delightful.

The Northern Cotswolds Loop

Start from Broadway, often called the jewel of the Cotswolds. Head south through Stanton and Stanway — two impossibly pretty villages — to Winchcombe. Continue via Sudeley Castle to Cheltenham, then loop back through Stow-on-the-Wold and Chipping Campden. This 50-mile loop takes in the classic Cotswolds experience.

The Southern Cotswolds Circuit

From Cirencester, ride west through Bibury (with its famous Arlington Row), past Barnsley and Burford to the Windrush Valley. Continue through Minster Lovell and Witney, then south through Lechlade and back to Cirencester. The roads are gentle and the villages are perfectly preserved — like riding through a period drama.

Must-Visit Cotswolds Villages

  • Castle Combe — Regularly voted England's prettiest village, tucked in a wooded valley
  • Bibury — William Morris called it the most beautiful village in England
  • Bourton-on-the-Water — The Venice of the Cotswolds, with stone bridges over the Windrush
  • Stow-on-the-Wold — Historic market square perfect for a lunch stop
  • Painswick — Queen of the Cotswolds, famous for its yew-lined churchyard
The Cotswolds rewards slow riding and frequent stops. Park up, explore a village on foot, have cream tea, and remember that motorcycling isn't always about the bends.

The Best Cotswolds Roads

The B4632 from Broadway to Cheltenham follows the escarpment edge with views across the Vale of Evesham — one of the most scenic B-roads in England. The A436 from Cheltenham to Stow crosses high wold country with long views and flowing bends. For something quieter, the minor roads through the Slaughters (Upper and Lower Slaughter) are narrow and magical.

Practical Information

The Cotswolds is well-served with fuel, food, and accommodation. Tourist traffic can be heavy in summer, especially at honey-pot villages like Bourton-on-the-Water and Broadway. Ride midweek or in spring and autumn for the best experience. Road surfaces are excellent — the Cotswolds benefits from Gloucestershire and Oxfordshire's well-maintained road network. The area is easily accessible from London (90 minutes), Birmingham (1 hour), and Bristol (45 minutes).

When to Visit

The Cotswolds is beautiful year-round. Spring brings lambs and wildflowers, summer delivers long days and garden fetes, autumn turns the beech woods golden, and even winter has its charms with frost on the stone walls and log fires in the pubs. faq.q: What kind of riding does the Cotswolds offer?
faq.a: The Cotswolds is touring at its most civilised, with gentle, flowing roads through honey-stone villages, rolling farmland and ancient market towns. It is a complete contrast to the mountain passes elsewhere in Britain, rewarding a relaxed pace, frequent stops and an appreciation of understated English beauty.

faq.q: Which villages are worth stopping at?
faq.a: Castle Combe is regularly voted England's prettiest village, Bibury was called the most beautiful in England by William Morris, and Bourton-on-the-Water is known as the Venice of the Cotswolds. Stow-on-the-Wold suits a lunch stop, while Painswick is famous for its yew-lined churchyard.

faq.q: When should I ride the Cotswolds?
faq.a: The Cotswolds is beautiful year-round, but tourist traffic can be heavy in summer, especially at honey-pot villages like Bourton-on-the-Water and Broadway.
